Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - testEscapedQuote_LANG_477 creates an ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom registry and the pattern: "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!".
  - It doesn’t call format(); the failure is triggered during construction because the constructor calls applyPattern.

- Relevant constructor path:
  - ExtendedMessageFormat(String, Map) delegates to ExtendedMessageFormat(String, Locale, Map).
  - In this constructor, applyPattern(pattern) is invoked when a registry is provided (lines 123–128).

- Where parsing happens:
  - applyPattern(String) handles custom registry patterns manually (lines 142–206). It loops over the pattern characters and:
    - On QUOTE ('): calls appendQuotedString(pattern, pos, stripCustom, true) (line 158).
    - On default characters: appends the char and advances the position (lines 187–189).

- The bug:
  - appendQuotedString(String, ParsePosition, StringBuffer, boolean) has an early-return branch (lines 421–423):
    - If escapingOn is true and the current character is a quote, it simply appends a single quote to appendTo and returns without advancing the ParsePosition.
  - In applyPattern, after calling appendQuotedString for QUOTE, there is no position advancement in that switch case; it relies on appendQuotedString to move the position.
  - Because the early return does not move pos, the outer while loop sees the same QUOTE again and again. Each iteration:
    - Hits the QUOTE case,
    - Calls appendQuotedString, which appends another quote and returns,
    - Leaves pos unchanged.

- Why OutOfMemory occurs:
  - This creates an infinite loop appending quotes to stripCustom, causing the buffer to grow until an OutOfMemoryError is thrown.
  - This behavior is only triggered when a registry is provided, because without a registry applyPattern delegates to the JDK’s MessageFormat (lines 143–147), avoiding this custom parsing code. This matches the issue summary (“with custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes, an OutOfMemoryError will occur”).

- How the pattern triggers it:
  - The test pattern contains an escaped quote sequence in "it''s". At the first of the adjacent quotes, appendQuotedString is invoked with escapingOn=true.
  - Instead of recognizing and consuming the escaped quote (two consecutive quotes) or a quoted block, the early return appends a quote and fails to advance pos, leading to the infinite loop described above.
  - Notably, the rest of appendQuotedString actually contains correct logic to handle escaped quotes (lines 426–431) and quoted blocks (lines 433–440), but that logic is never reached because of the premature return at lines 421–423.

- Summary:
  - The OutOfMemoryError and the failing test are caused by appendQuotedString’s early return when encountering a quote with escaping enabled, which appends a quote but does not advance the parse position. This stalls the parser in applyPattern’s loop, resulting in infinite appends and memory exhaustion.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
